instruction: There's a flipped video on the Desktop. Please use VLC to rotate it correctly (180 degrees), then save it on the Desktop with the filename 'MacintoshCommercial.mp4'.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires agent to rotate the flipped video 180 degrees in VLC and save it as 'MacintoshCommercial.mp4' on Desktop. Evaluator checks if the output file exists at the expected location. Similar to original task pattern but with different output filename and state-based evaluation.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: file existence, correct filename, video validity, and proper rotation
Getter (getters/file.py:147-160) correctly extracts rotation metadata from both source and output videos using ffprobe
Getter correctly sets rotation_changed=True ONLY for 180->0 transformation (correcting flipped video to normal)
Metric (metrics/file.py:83-85) correctly accepts ONLY 180->0 transformation (source flipped, output normal)
Metric (metrics/file.py:92-94) correctly rejects 0->180 transformation (would make normal video flipped - wrong direction)
Metric (metrics/file.py:88-90) correctly rejects same-rotation scenarios (prevents simple file copy without rotation)
Metric (metrics/file.py:96-99) correctly verifies 180-degree rotation difference for other cases
Logic semantically matches instruction: 'flipped video' (rotation=180) 'rotate correctly (180 degrees)' -> normal video (rotation=0)
Comprehensive validation: checks file existence, video validity, minimum size (100KB), and correct rotation transformation
Edge cases handled: invalid videos, empty files, missing rotation metadata, and incorrect rotation directions
